specApproval: not obtained (autonomous run); user authorized fixing the investigated bug

setup.dependencies: No new dependencies; use existing Node, PostgreSQL, fast-check, c8, ESLint and TypeScript.
setup.isolation: Standard docker-compose.mbt-test.yml, unique project, mbbs-tests.slice, existing bounded settings, teardown registered before startup.
setup.git: Preserve unrelated work; no commits or branch changes.
setup.deployment: One-file overlay on the captured live app image, exact candidate verification, app-only restart with automatic rollback, no database migrations or NetSuite writes.
setup.artifacts: Persist regression tests, runner, mutation script, source hashes, logs and evidence; remove all disposable test resources.
setup.savedSearch: After the correction, provide a read-only SuiteScript method for customsearch503. Do not switch the production balance source.

acceptance: P1 A synthetic customer with 194 fulfilled and credited at one yard and 12 fulfilled at another has fulfilled=206, returned=194 and available=12, despite accounting mirror rows and one actual 7-pallet main line.
P2 A 7-pallet fulfillment whose actual item row has mainline=T still contributes exactly 7.
P3 A 5-pallet fulfillment and 2-pallet credit memo, each accompanied by accounting rows, yield fulfilled=5 and returned=2.
P4 Generated positive and fractional movements across yards conserve actual fulfilled/credited quantities regardless of accounting rows, fulfillment mainline flag or input order.
P5 Other customers, other items, tax lines and void/cancel/reject statuses do not contribute; customer-wide scope and credit memo identity remain intact.
P6 Invalid customer/item identifiers fail before a query can execute.
R1 Existing return, credit memo, authorization, pending reservation, duplicate-credit, freshness, authorization and concurrency regressions have zero new failures.
R2 The endpoint and balance response shape stay compatible, including available=max(fulfilled-returned-localReserved,0).
L1 The deployed production function independently returns fulfilled=206, netsuiteReturned=194 and available=12 for customer 5240 when the source transactions remain unchanged.

failureModel.risk: Counting accounting mirrors overstates return entitlement
failureModel.check: Execute generated production SQL against synthetic transaction tables; targeted mutations and generated conservation cases.

failureModel.risk: Discarding real main lines understates entitlement
failureModel.check: Mainline=T regression, generated mainline choices, and live REST-verified historical fulfillment.

failureModel.risk: Changing customer, item, status or yard scope
failureModel.check: Adversarial decoy records and all affected return regressions.

failureModel.risk: Releasing a pending return or accepting a duplicate concurrent return
failureModel.check: Existing return reservation, freshness and concurrency tests; repository code unchanged.

failureModel.risk: Deploying unrelated workspace changes or interrupting an active posting
failureModel.check: Captured live image, one-file hash comparison, active-operation preflight, rollback and health checks.

validationLimits: PostgreSQL executes the same generated SQL with only NVL translated to COALESCE and BUILTIN.DF(status) mapped to fixture status text; a live read-only SuiteQL query verifies the NetSuite dialect.
Run the complete affected return-domain suite rather than the unrelated whole-application suite; record all selected files and any baseline failures.
Existing module-wide type/lint findings must be compared against the captured baseline. No new findings are allowed.
No performance SLA is introduced; record live lookup duration without imposing an arbitrary budget.
